card: Enables 13 additional clang-tidy bugprone checks and fixes existing violations in Qt and unit test code. Changes include using C++20 std::erase in WalletController, adding a LIFETIMEBOUND annotation in notificator.cpp, and fixing test strings with embedded NUL bytes. The author reports that the checks revealed no severe bugs in production code, but enabling them in CI prevents future defects.
changed_since_previous: No substantive changes to the code or scope; rebased commits.
evidence: Author description: 'Apart from a test-only bug, they didn't find anything severe, but I think it still makes sense to enable them, so that it is easier to read the resulting code.'
problem: Clang-tidy does not enforce various bugprone checks, leaving the codebase vulnerable to silent regressions like dangling handles, inaccurate container erasure, string truncation from embedded NULs, and missing lifetime annotations.

risk.why: Changes are confined to linter rules, unit test literals, and safe Qt container/lifetime adjustments with no effect on consensus or network logic.

scope_notes: Touches linter configuration and a few isolated lines across Qt and unit tests.
summary: Enables 13 additional clang-tidy bugprone checks in `.clang-tidy` and resolves existing violations. Adjustments include using C++20 `std::erase` in Qt wallet controller, adding a `LIFETIMEBOUND` annotation in `notificator.cpp`, marking an unused RAII variable in a unit test, and using explicit `std::string_view`/`std::string` literals for strings with embedded NULs in utility tests.
